author: OpenAI
text: 🎉 Congratulations to the GPT-3 team for earning a Best Paper Award this morning at #NeurIPS2020! https://t.co/Gvc5brkZ5z

author: OpenAI
text: Join us at NeurIPS 2020 to learn more about OpenAI's research, including live demos of GPT-3: https://t.co/Gvc5brkZ5z

author: OpenAI
text: We've used reinforcement learning from human feedback to train language models for summarization. The resulting models produce better summaries than 10x larger models trained only with supervised learning: https://t.co/Sk31d1CnTu

author: OpenAI
text: Applications are now open for our Fall 2020 Scholars program, which supports underrepresented groups in STEM to study deep learning full-time for 6 months. Apply here: https://t.co/pIvZkJXO6p

author: OpenAI
text: We recognize these issues are complex; as an industry we need to work together to improve the way we tackle them. New projects that expand OpenAI’s work in these critical areas are underway, building on existing work in the field. Research & product outputs to come. 8/8

author: OpenAI
text: We’re deploying a content filtration system as a starting point to allow a developer to control what content can be returned. Technology alone won't be the answer; we're working with users and our Academic Access partners for a more comprehensive approach. 7/8

author: OpenAI
text: Before applications go live, they’re also subject to a review with the OpenAI team. Our technical enforcement is catching up to our policies, and the process is improving. We still have many policies to create. 6/8

author: OpenAI
text: As we gain more experience operating the API in practice we expect to expand and refine these categories. We’re actively enforcing our terms of use. 5/8

author: OpenAI
text: We’ve shared API Usage Guidelines w/ users that include heuristics for safely developing applications. We do not support use cases which may cause physical or mental harm, including but not limited to harassment, intentional deception, radicalization, astroturfing, or spam. 4/8

author: OpenAI
text: Generative models can display both overt and diffuse harmful outputs, such as racist, sexist, or otherwise pernicious language. This is an industry-wide issue, making it easy for individual organizations to abdicate or defer responsibility. OpenAI will not. 3/8

author: OpenAI
text: We rolled out limited access to the API via a private beta, which is a way for us to understand the challenges of deploying open-ended generative models in the real world, but with mechanisms in place for safety. 2/8

author: OpenAI
text: Last month we released an API for developers to build on top of our latest technology: https://t.co/4BaTBWzRtQ. There’s been a lot of enthusiasm, but a great deal needs to be figured out as we scale up access. Here's how we're thinking about it. 1/8

quoted.text: We're releasing an API for accessing new AI models developed by OpenAI. You can "program" the API in natural language with just a few examples of your task. See how companies are using the API today, or join our waitlist: https://t.co/SvTgaFuTzN https://t.co/uoeeuqpDWR

author: OpenAI
text: Over the past 5 months our 3rd class of Scholars researched how GPT-2 represents grammar, measured the interpretability of models trained on Coinrun, predicted epileptic seizures using brain recordings and more: https://t.co/XmKfSgdLB1

author: OpenAI
text: We're proud to support the National Research Cloud initiative to direct more computation to academia: https://t.co/gybBQ6tqkZ

author: OpenAI
text: We found that just as a large transformer model trained on language can generate coherent text, the same exact model trained on pixel sequences can generate coherent image completions and samples. https://t.co/whREMuBvxx https://t.co/6AGsfx26gM

author: OpenAI
text: We're co-organizing two NeurIPS 2020 competitions using Procgen Benchmark and MineRL. We rely heavily on these environments internally for RL research, and we look forward to seeing the progress the community makes in these challenging competitions. https://t.co/ROe3zGAbwC

author: OpenAI
text: It’s not enough for a company to be non-racist or to tweet Black Lives Matter. We want to be actively anti-racist, and to do that we need to make proactive corrections when it comes to sharing space and opportunity. We’re committed to doing the work. (4/4)

author: OpenAI
text: At OpenAI our aim is to ensure that advanced AI systems of the future are built to benefit everyone. That means we need to work harder to diversify our employees too. We’ve not done a good enough job on this to date. (3/4)

author: OpenAI
text: We’re significantly expanding the number of Scholars, and we’d be excited if all additional slots go to members of the Black community, whom we will heavily recruit. We’ll share details in the coming weeks for this next class of Scholars. (2/4)

author: OpenAI
text: We’ve been talking at OpenAI about what we can do to help Black equity. We’re committing $1M to this cause via direct donations and expanding our Scholars program, which provides educational resources and mentoring to underrepresented groups in AI. (1/4)

author: OpenAI
text: Our 3rd cohort of Scholars are wrapping up their final projects and we'd like to connect them with great companies in AI. If you're currently hiring ML researchers/engineers, fill out this form to participate in our (virtual) speed interview day June 17th! https://t.co/gLUq7vAXMV https://t.co/Uwb3ZCa06p

author: OpenAI
text:
Since 2012, the amount of compute for training to AlexNet-level performance on ImageNet has been decreasing exponentially — halving every 16 months, in total a 44x improvement. 

By contrast, Moore's Law would only have yielded an 11x cost improvement: https://t.co/nQnZ4uPXQf https://t.co/vRwfm2UlSq

author: OpenAI
text: Introducing Jukebox, a neural net that generates music, including rudimentary singing, as raw audio in a variety of genres and artist styles. We're releasing a tool for everyone to explore the generated samples, as well as the model and code: https://t.co/EUq7hNZv62 https://t.co/sh5yHz7qrc

author: OpenAI
text: We've contributed to a multi-stakeholder report by 58 co-authors at 30 organizations that describes 10 mechanisms to improve the verifiability of claims made about AI systems. https://t.co/Wxz0BY3qR5

author: OpenAI
text: Introducing OpenAI Microscope: a collection of visualizations of every layer and neuron in eight vision "model organisms" often studied in interpretability. This tool allows researchers to investigate down to individual units, and share those observations. https://t.co/9RxZwc5DOR

author: OpenAI
text: We're hiring a senior technical recruiter to join our People Ops team! You'll develop, iterate on, and manage recruiting processes and systems from end-to-end; also source, pitch, screen and close top talent for our research org. Interested? Please apply! https://t.co/EkvMsmNVbK

author: OpenAI
text: Want to participate in Circuits? Or just want a sneak peek into the next article? You can join the Distill slack circuits channel at https://t.co/HTxMxjs1cr

author: OpenAI
text: This post, called Zoom In, is the first in a new series called Circuits. Over the course of the series, we and our collaborators will flesh out how we think neural nets can be understood and explained.

author: OpenAI
text: We show how to read a human-interpretable algorithm from a neural network's weights, by studying the circuits formed by the connections between individual neurons: https://t.co/oX47rfEmqx https://t.co/YPtrowyt5k
